rules.desc:
Elective courses to meet the 60 unit major minimum can be taken within the following parameters.

• Coursework within the department. Additional ITALIAN courses taught by Italian faculty (may be taught in English or Italian) at the 100- or 200-level.

• Language coursework. Up to three language courses in Italian at or above ITALLANG 21, such as ITALLANG22 and 23 or ITALIAN 21A and 22A for a maximum of 12 units may apply to the major.

• Coursework in other departments relevant to the degree, on Italian topics, with the approval of the Director of Undergraduate Studies.

• Bing Overseas Study Program. Courses taken at the Bing Overseas Studies in Florence program with prior approval of the Director of Undergraduate Studies.

• Education as Self-Fashioning courses taught at least partially by a French and Italian Department faculty member. Students may count a maximum of ten units.

• Structured Liberal Education. Students may count ten units of SLE coursework towards their major elective totals.

• Digital Humanities Course. Student work must reflect Italian interests. Prior approval of the Director of Undergraduate Studies. Maximum of five units.

• Independent Study. No more than 12 units of coursework for the major should be taken as independent study courses.
*Italian & Philosophy subplan elective details are listed within the subplan section.

Students majoring in any DLCL department (i.e., Comparative Literature, French and Italian, German Studies, Iberian and Latin American Cultures, and Slavic Languages and Literatures) who have an overall grade point average (GPA) of 3.3 or above and who maintain a 3.5 (GPA) in their major courses, are eligible to participate in the DLCL’s honors program.
See the Honors webpage for more information.
Program Requirements
To earn honors, students must complete a minimum of 9 units, submit a thesis, and present at the Honors Colloquium at the end of their senior year.

rules.name: Italian and Philosophy Subplan Policies:
rules.desc:
• The Italian and Philosophy subplan requires 66 units. Students interested in this option should review the Philosophy and Literature website.

• Up to ten units of courses taken in the Philosophy department may be taken ‘CR/NC’ or ‘S/NC’; the remainder must be taken for a letter grade.

• Substitutions and transfer credits are generally not permitted for the PHIL 170 series class or the PHIL 180 series class and are never allowed for PHIL 80, ITALIAN 181, or the capstone seminar.

• Once a student has completed the SLE sequence (all three quarters), they may count up to 10 units towards this major. The SLE units can replace one history of philosophy course and one upper-division Italian course.

Program Requirements

children.name: 5,000-word Topic Paper
children.desc:
The student will write a 5,000-word paper on a topic of their choosing, serving as the culmination of their work in the field.
To write the paper, students must enroll in a 3-unit, letter-grade independent study with a faculty member (or affiliate) in the Philosophy and Literature Focal Group. The paper must involve philosophy and literature, and the faculty member must approve the topic by the add/drop deadline.

gpa: A grade point average (GPA) of 2.0 or better must be achieved in each course.
grading:
All courses applied to the Italian Culture and Literature subplans must be taken for a letter grade and passed with at least a ‘C’.
Italian and Philosophy Subplan: Up to ten units of courses taken in the Philosophy department may be taken ‘CR/NC’ or ‘S/NC’; the remainder must be taken for a letter grade.
policies: These 60 units may not be used for any other major or minor.
transferPolicy:
The department may accept up to 12 units of transfer credit toward the major with approval from the Director of Undergraduate Studies.
Italian and Philosophy Subplan: Substitutions and transfer credits are generally not permitted for the PHIL 170 series class or the PHIL 180 series class and are never allowed for PHIL 80, ITALIAN 181, or the capstone seminar.

reviewNotes: You choose the Italian Culture, Italian Literature, or Italian and Philosophy subplan. The audit checks the 60 units (66 with Italian and Philosophy), the subplan's courses, WIM and capstone, and electives from 100- and 200-level ITALIAN courses, up to three Italian language courses at or above ITALLANG 21 (12 units) and up to 10 SLE units, with at most 12 units of ITALIAN 199. Every course needs a C or better and a letter grade, except up to 10 PHIL units in the Philosophy subplan. Checked by hand: the OPI, ITALLANG 22A or the equivalent, which courses were taught in Italian, electives from other departments, Bing Overseas Florence, ESF and Digital Humanities, transfer units (up to 12 with approval) and the honors thesis.
